candidates.explanation: The soft-delete excludes the wrong value. It uses `id: Not(Number(conditions.userId))`, which compares the session id column to the user id. It should compare it to `conditions.excludeSessionId`. The caller's current session is therefore not protected, so it gets deleted and the next refresh returns 401. A different session whose id happens to equal the user id is kept instead, which is why an unrelated older session sometimes survives. The visible snippet doesn't show whether the query is also scoped to the user, so that needs checking too.

This is the Mongo counterpart. The snippet is truncated, so I couldn't confirm it. If its `_id: { $not: ... }` or `$ne` filter uses the same wrong value, it has the same bug. Check that it excludes `excludeSessionId` and filters by `user: userId`.

fix.description: In SessionRelationalRepository.deleteByUserIdWithExclude, change the filter to `user: { id: Number(conditions.userId) }, id: Not(Number(conditions.excludeSessionId))`. Check that the document repository's filter also excludes `excludeSessionId`.
